$comment: Lighthouse CI. Run locally with `npx lhci autorun`, and in the lighthouse job in CI.
What is asserted as an error is what a shared CI runner can measure reliably:
accessibility, best practices, and layout shift. Those are properties of the markup
and the stylesheet, and they come out the same on any machine.
Performance and LCP are warnings, and that is deliberate rather than a shrug. A
GitHub runner is a shared virtual machine whose CPU is contended; the same build
measured 87 and 91 on this project's own laptop depending on what else was running,
and a budget that fails for that reason teaches everyone to ignore it. The numbers
are still collected and reported on every run, so a real regression is visible.
docs/QA.md records the medians measured on a quiet machine, which is the honest
SEO is a warning for one specific reason: the site is deliberately noindex until
launch, which costs the is-crawlable audit and caps the category at about 66. With
NEXT_PUBLIC_INDEXABLE=true the same build scores 100 with nothing failing. Part 17
turns it on, and this becomes an error assertion then.
